subject: chemistry_2
question_text: Draw the structures of the following: i) Serotonin ii) Bithionol iii) Chloramphenicol iv) Saccharin

verification.note: The 1+1+1+1 mark split is a CLAIM, not the board's, until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented. Unit 14 (Chemistry in Everyday Life) is sourced from the chemistry half of "FAST TRACK IPE for Sr. Students", book pp.105-106, printed chapter "11. CHEMISTRY IN EVERYDAY LIFE"; the book prints this question on book p.106 as SAQ 3, with the four structures drawn beside it. Neither the two-book union check nor a board back-test was possible for Chemistry-II: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is physics-only and first-year, and no second-year chemistry paper is in the corpus. FIGURE SCOPE: the printed question says "Draw the structures", so the drawings ARE the marked work and each diagram step carries one mark. The names written in words carry none and the first step is therefore marks 0. All four structures are drawn: each is a single ring or a fused pair of rings with substituents, and each fits inside the sixteen element limit with room to spare, so none of them had to be written as a named description instead. The renderer draws outlines only, so every ring is given its own clear lane and no bond passes behind a label. BOOK STRUCTURE CHECKED (book p.106): serotonin is drawn by the book with the OH on the benzene ring and CH2CH2NH2 on the five membered ring, with N-H at the bottom, which is correct for 5-hydroxytryptamine; bithionol is drawn as two dichlorophenol rings joined by one sulphur atom, which is correct for 2,2'-thiobis(4,6-dichlorophenol); chloramphenicol is drawn as O2N-C6H4-CH(OH)-CH(NHCOCHCl2)-CH2OH, which is correct; saccharin is drawn as a benzene ring fused to a five membered ring carrying C=O, NH and SO2, which is correct. No error was found in the four printed structures. SPELLING RECORDED: NCERT prints this antiseptic as "bithional"; the accepted name is bithionol, which is what this book prints and what the card uses. The book gives no chemical name for any of them; the names are added in the first step and in the figure captions so the drawings can be checked against something.

steps.why: The question asks for drawings, so these lines earn nothing on their own. They are written first because a structure drawn from a description is far easier to check than one drawn from memory, and because a student who runs out of time can still show the examiner that the compound was known.
common_mistakes: Spending the whole answer on words. The question says draw, and only the drawings are marked.
Writing a molecular formula in place of a structure. C₇H₅NO₃S tells the examiner nothing about how the atoms are joined.
steps.memory_tip: Two of the four are fused ring systems, serotonin and saccharin; the other two are a single ring or a pair of rings joined by one atom.
steps.margin_note: These lines earn no marks. All four marks sit on the four drawings, so keep this part short.

steps.label: Serotonin

elements.text: Serotonin — OH at 5, side chain at 3

steps.why: Serotonin is 5-hydroxytryptamine. The skeleton is indole: a benzene ring fused to a five membered ring that carries the nitrogen atom. The OH goes on the benzene ring at position 5 and the CH₂CH₂NH₂ side chain goes on the five membered ring at position 3, next to the fused edge. Getting those two positions right is the whole of this mark.
common_mistakes: Drawing a single benzene ring. Serotonin has two fused rings, and the nitrogen sits in the smaller one.
Putting the side chain on the benzene ring. It is attached to the five membered ring, at the carbon next to the fused edge.
steps.memory_tip: Indole plus one OH plus one CH₂CH₂NH₂: two rings, two substituents, nothing else.
steps.margin_note: Draw the fused pair of rings first, then add the N–H, then the two substituents. Label them; an unlabelled ring earns nothing.

steps.label: Bithionol

elements.text: Bithionol — two rings joined by one S

steps.why: Bithionol is 2,2'-thiobis(4,6-dichlorophenol). Each ring is a phenol: the OH is position 1, the sulphur bridge is at position 2 beside it, and the two chlorine atoms are at positions 4 and 6. The two rings are identical and are joined by one sulphur atom, so the picture is a mirror image about the sulphur.
common_mistakes: Joining the two rings by an oxygen atom. The bridge is sulphur; the name begins with thio.
Drawing one chlorine atom per ring. Each ring carries two, at positions 4 and 6.
steps.memory_tip: Two of everything: two rings, two OH groups, four Cl atoms, one S in the middle.
steps.margin_note: Draw one ring completely, then copy it as a mirror image. Two OH and four Cl labels must all appear.

steps.label: Chloramphenicol
steps.why: Chloramphenicol is one benzene ring carrying a nitro group, joined to a three carbon chain. The nitro group and the chain are para to each other, at opposite corners of the ring. The middle carbon of the chain carries the NHCOCHCl₂ group, the first carbon carries OH and the last is CH₂OH. Two chlorine atoms are on the acid part of the amide, which is what the name records.
common_mistakes: Putting the nitro group ortho or meta to the chain. It is para, at the opposite corner.
Writing NHCOCH₂Cl with one chlorine. There are two chlorine atoms: NHCOCHCl₂.
steps.memory_tip: Nitro at one end, CH₂OH at the other, and the two chlorine atoms on the amide in the middle.
steps.margin_note: The three carbon chain must show all three carbons with their own groups. Count the chlorine atoms before finishing.

steps.label: Saccharin

elements.text: Saccharin — C(=O), NH and SO₂ ring

steps.why: Saccharin is a benzene ring fused to a five membered ring. Going round the small ring from the top fused carbon: a carbon carrying the double bonded oxygen, then NH, then the sulphur with its two double bonded oxygen atoms, and back to the lower fused carbon. The three oxygen atoms, one on carbon and two on sulphur, are what a student most often leaves out.
common_mistakes: Drawing only one oxygen atom on the sulphur. There are two, and the group is SO₂.
Putting the NH next to the benzene ring. The order round the small ring is C(=O), then NH, then SO₂.
steps.memory_tip: Three oxygen atoms in all: one on the carbon, two on the sulphur, with the NH between them.
steps.margin_note: Count three oxygen atoms and one NH before finishing. That count is what the examiner checks first.

insider_note: All four marks sit on the four drawings, one each, so draw before writing. Label every atom that is not a plain ring carbon; an unlabelled ring earns nothing, and the oxygen count on saccharin and the chlorine count on bithionol and chloramphenicol are what the examiner checks first.
